span.label: THE VOCABULARY OF CHILDREN'S LANGUAGE PROBLEMS, DECIDED BY DELPHI - 57 panellists across six English-speaking countries and eight professions rating 21 statements over two rounds, with every agreement percentage published and the two failing items named
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: what to call language problems in children, when the most frequent term in the research literature is the one the panel most disagrees about, and when the label decides whether a child gets a service
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: twelve consensus statements: `language disorder` defined by functional impact and prognosis rather than by test cut-offs, `developmental language disorder` for cases with no known biomedical cause, and exclusionary criteria replaced by a threefold distinction
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: method
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a field in which the same child receives four different diagnoses depending on which professional sees them, and in which a term's exclusion criteria had become grounds for refusing services
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a two-round online Delphi with anonymised feedback, a one-day meeting between rounds, moderators who did not rate, and a statistical test of whether agreement tracked profession or country
span.term: a two-round online Delphi with anonymised feedback, a one-day meeting between rounds, moderators who did not rate, and a statistical test of whether agreement tracked profession or country

span.label: **A TERM ABOLISHED RATHER THAN REDEFINED, WITH THE COST OF DOING SO PRINTED**: `The term SPECIFIC LANGUAGE IMPAIRMENT, WHICH WAS THE MOST FREQUENT IN THE RESEARCH LITERATURE, was the subject of substantial disagreement ... ULTIMATELY, THE DECISION WAS MADE TO REJECT THE TERM. A MAJOR DRAWBACK ... is that IT CREATES A DISCONTINUITY WITH PRIOR LITERATURE, WHICH COULD AFFECT FUTURE META-ANALYSES AND SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS ... RATHER THAN REDEFINING THE TERM, IT WOULD BE BETTER TO ABOLISH IT.` **Four bodies in this corpus heard the continuity argument and kept a term they called suboptimal. This one heard it and went the other way** [CORRECTED 2026-08-23 by terminal-a. **THE COUNT IS THREE, NOT FOUR**, and the same correction was applied to `concept_edges[1].note` earlier today and MISSED THIS FIELD - the record has been stating three and four about itself ever since, which CLAUDE_B caught. The three, named so the claim can be re-run: `cruz-jentoft2010` (`THE TERM DYNAPENIA IS BETTER SUITED ... however SARCOPENIA IS ALREADY A WIDELY RECOGNISED TERM, SO REPLACING IT MIGHT LEAD TO FURTHER CONFUSION`), `buck2011` (`a PRAGMATIC COMPROMISE between IUPAC/CAS nomenclature, internal consistency and existing LEGACY USAGE`) and `bronte2016` (`THE TERM MDSC MAY NOT BE OPTIMAL ... SHOULD BE RETAINED TO ASSURE CONSISTENCY`). The fourth I counted was `staab2017` keeping PPV, SMD, VV and CSD as ICD-11 INDEX TERMS - preserving RETIRED names as cross-references, which is not keeping a suboptimal term IN USE. **A cross-record count in a prose field is a claim about the corpus that nothing in the corpus checks**, which is why it is now written with its members. The superseded sentence is kept verbatim above rather than deleted.]
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE CONSENSUS THRESHOLD ITSELF HAS NO AGREED VALUE, SAID BEFORE ONE IS CHOSEN**: `THERE IS NO AGREED CRITERION FOR WHEN A DELPHI CONSENSUS IS DEEMED ADEQUATE for an item - in the literature, VALUES FROM 51% TO 80% AGREEMENT HAVE BEEN USED. WE AIMED FOR 75% AGREEMENT AS A REASONABLE GOAL.` staab2017 published a decision rule and then missed it. This one publishes that **the method has no rule**, declares 75% in advance, and reports at 78%
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE PANEL TESTED WHETHER ITS OWN AGREEMENT WAS AN ARTEFACT OF WHO WAS ON IT**: `Kruskal-Wallis tests were conducted on each item to test WHETHER AGREEMENT WAS RELATED TO EITHER GEOGRAPHICAL LOCATION (six countries) OR PROFESSIONAL STATUS ... NONE of these comparisons was statistically significant after correction ... GIVEN THE SMALL SAMPLE SIZE, WE CANNOT RULE OUT AN EFFECT.` A control on a definitional PROCESS rather than on a measurement - and the negative result is reported with its power caveat attached
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND A FAILURE OF CONSENSUS READ AS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE WORLD, NOT ABOUT THE PANEL**: `we FAILED TO REACH CONSENSUS about possible terminology for LINGUISTIC SUBTYPES of DLD. It is possible that as research advances the situation may change, BUT ANOTHER POSSIBILITY IS THAT IT IS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE PHENOMENON OF INTEREST: quite simply, CHILDREN WITH DLD DO NOT NEATLY DIVIDE INTO SUBTYPES along linguistic lines.` The two items that failed scored 68% and 46%, and both were about subtypes
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND ONE CHILD, FOUR DIAGNOSES, CHOSEN BY WHICH PROFESSIONAL IS IN THE ROOM**: `The terminology used for neurodevelopmental disorders can create the impression that there is a set of distinct conditions, BUT THE REALITY IS THAT MANY CHILDREN HAVE A MIXTURE OF PROBLEMS ... THE SAME CHILD MAY BE REGARDED AS HAVING DLD BY A SLT/P, DYSLEXIA BY A TEACHER, AUDITORY PROCESSING DISORDER BY AN AUDIOLOGIST, OR ADHD BY A PAEDIATRICIAN.` The label is a property of the observer
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND A DEFINITIONAL ELEMENT REMOVED FOR WHAT IT WAS BEING USED TO DO, NOT FOR BEING WRONG: `Panel members were concerned that, INSTEAD OF BEING USED FOR DIAGNOSTIC DIFFERENTIATION, EXCLUSIONARY CRITERIA WERE SOMETIMES INTERPRETED AS CRITERIA FOR DENYING SERVICES TO CHILDREN.` haas2018 deleted a word because it confused clinicians; this panel deleted a whole criterion TYPE because of what administrators did with it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE REPLACEMENT IS A THREE-WAY SPLIT WHERE THERE HAD BEEN A GATE: `RATHER THAN USING EXCLUSIONARY CRITERIA in the definition of language disorder, WE DRAW A THREEFOLD DISTINCTION between DIFFERENTIATING CONDITIONS, RISK FACTORS and CO-OCCURRING CONDITIONS.` Only the first is diagnostically exclusive; the other two are recorded and do not preclude the diagnosis
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE TWO OBJECTIONS TO THE CHOSEN MODIFIER POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: `Some panel members noted specific meanings of `DEVELOPMENTAL` THAT WERE NOT INTENDED: for example, THAT THIS WAS SOMETHING THAT THE CHILD MIGHT `GROW OUT OF`, OR - QUITE THE CONVERSE - THAT A DEVELOPMENTAL PROBLEM MEANT THAT THE CHILD WOULD BE UNABLE TO DEVELOP LANGUAGE.` **A modifier misread in two contradictory ways, and kept anyway** - because the alternatives (`primary`, `specific`) drew the same objection
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND `DISORDER` WAS PREFERRED TO `IMPAIRMENT` ON FOUR NAMED GROUNDS, WITH THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT PRINTED: for `the greater seriousness and importance associated with the term`, consistency with ASD/DCD/ADHD, and compatibility with DSM-5 and ICD-11 - against `concerns that the term `DISORDER` HAD MEDICAL CONNOTATIONS AND PLACED THE PROBLEM `INSIDE THE CHILD`, WHEN IT MIGHT BE CONTEXTUALLY DEPENDENT`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND A CATEGORY CREATED FOR ONE AUDIENCE AND EXPLICITLY DISCLAIMED FOR THE OTHERS**: SLCN is recommended because `THE NUMBER OF CHILDREN WITH SPECIFIC NEEDS ... HAS RESOURCE IMPLICATIONS`, and then: `IT IS NOT ANTICIPATED THAT THIS TERMINOLOGY WILL BE USEFUL FOR THOSE DOING RESEARCH on the nature or causes of language disorders, NOR WILL IT BE HELPFUL IN EXPLAINING A CHILD'S DIFFICULTIES TO PARENTS or in determining a treatment pathway.` A term with its audience written into it, and the non-audiences named
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE DELPHI'S OWN EFFECT IS MEASURED: round 1 agreement ran `FROM 30% TO 98% for the 16 items, WITH A MEDIAN VALUE OF 74%`; round 2 ran `FROM 46% TO 98% across items, WITH A MEDIAN VALUE OF 90%`. **The median moved 16 points between rounds**, with a one-day meeting and anonymised feedback in between
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE OLD NOSOLOGY IS DIAGNOSED BEFORE IT IS REPLACED: `it has in the past been based on information from A MIXTURE OF DIFFERENT LEVELS OF DESCRIPTION` - presenting severity, co-occurring nonlanguage problems, and putative biological or environmental causes - which `IMPLIES THAT THE CONSTELLATION of verbal and nonverbal skills WILL MAP ONTO NATURAL SUBTYPES WITH DISTINCT CAUSES ... HOWEVER, THIS APPROACH HAS NOT WORKED.` A classification built on three incommensurable axes at once
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE PANEL IS ENGLISH-ONLY AND SAYS SO: `An obvious limitation of this study is that WE RESTRICTED OUR FOCUS TO THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE because of the difficulties of devising terms that would be applicable across different language and cultures.` The recommended remedy is the method, not the terms - `WE RECOMMEND THE USE OF THE DELPHI METHOD TO RESEARCHERS WORKING WITH LANGUAGE DISORDERS IN OTHER LANGUAGES`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE PANEL IS DOMINATED BY ONE PROFESSION: 57 individuals, of whom 31 are speech-language therapists or pathologists and 7 more are joint SLT/psychologists - so two thirds of the raters share a training. `NINE PANEL MEMBERS HAD A CLOSE RELATIVE WITH IMPAIRED LANGUAGE DEVELOPMENT`, which is disclosed and not adjusted for
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE CENTRAL BOUNDARY IS CONCEDED NOT TO EXIST: `THERE IS NO CLEAR DIVIDING LINE BETWEEN NORMALITY AND DISORDER; third, within the domain of language, CHILDREN'S PROBLEMS DO NOT NEATLY SEGREGATE INTO SUBTYPES, and there may be overlap between problems in speech, language and communication.` The definition that follows is therefore built on PROGNOSIS and FUNCTIONAL IMPACT rather than on a cut-off
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE ALTERNATIVE THE DEFINITION REFUSES IS NAMED: `it cautions against DEFINING LANGUAGE DISORDER SOLELY IN TERMS OF STATISTICAL CUT-OFFS ON LANGUAGE TESTS. Note also that WE REJECT ANY ATTEMPT TO USE DISCREPANCY SCORES to draw a distinction between `disorder` and `delay`: THE TERM `LANGUAGE DELAY` WAS WIDELY REJECTED BY OUR PANEL MEMBERS AS CONFUSING AND ILLOGICAL.` A second term abolished, in one clause, with no vote reported for it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Kruskal-Wallis tests on every item for an effect of geographical location (six countries) or professional status (SLT/P vs. others), Bonferroni-corrected at .001
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that the consensus is an artefact of who was recruited to the panel rather than of the subject matter · outcome: partial
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: two rating rounds with anonymised distributions and comments fed back between them, plus a one-day meeting attended by 22 panellists and 23 additional stakeholders
span.note: eliminates: a consensus that is just the first-round wording · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reporting the two items that failed to reach the threshold, with their agreement percentages, instead of dropping them
span.note: eliminates: a consensus document that reads as if everything was agreed · outcome: failed

span.label: `language disorder` (this paper) - problems `LIKELY TO ENDURE INTO MIDDLE CHILDHOOD AND BEYOND, WITH A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT on everyday social interactions or educational progress`; defined by PROGNOSIS and FUNCTION, explicitly not by a test cut-off and not by a verbal/nonverbal discrepancy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `developmental` (this paper's sense) - `the condition EMERGES IN THE COURSE OF DEVELOPMENT, rather than being acquired or associated with a known biomedical cause`; NOT `the child might grow out of it` and NOT `unable to develop language`, both of which panel members read into it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `SLCN` - a superordinate category recommended FOR POLICYMAKERS AND SERVICE PLANNERS ONLY, and disclaimed for researchers, for parents and for treatment planning in the same paragraph
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `specific` (in Specific Language Impairment) - a modifier the panel abolished rather than redefined, because it `HAD CONNOTATIONS THAT WERE MISLEADING AND CONFUSING` and because the discrepancy reading it invited was `DISCREDITED`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → CATALISE phase 1 (Bishop et al. 2016), which used the same panel to agree CRITERIA for identifying language problems; this second phase takes the TERMINOLOGY
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → the term `specific language impairment` - abolished rather than redefined, because `specific` `HAD CONNOTATIONS THAT WERE MISLEADING AND CONFUSING`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → DSM-5's social (pragmatic) communication disorder, considered for adoption and declined on two stated grounds
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → nosologies built on a mixture of levels of description - presenting severity, co-occurring nonlanguage problems and putative causes at once - which `HAS NOT WORKED`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: DLD —part-of→ SLCN
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `Quotation withheld.` The two terms exist for different readers - SLCN is recommended for policymakers and DISCLAIMED for researchers and parents in the same paragraph, so the containment is also a statement about AUDIENCE, which no field of ours records
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `THE TERM SPECIFIC LANGUAGE IMPAIRMENT, WHICH WAS THE MOST FREQUENT IN THE RESEARCH LITERATURE, was the subject of substantial disagreement among the panel ... RATHER THAN REDEFINING THE TERM, IT WOULD BE BETTER TO ABOLISH IT.` **The corpus has four bodies that kept a suboptimal term for continuity and this is the first that refused to.** [CORRECTED 2026-08-23 by terminal-a, after CLAUDE_B could not verify it and said so: **THE COUNT IS THREE, NOT FOUR.** The three, named so the claim can be re-run: `cruz-jentoft2010` (`THE TERM DYNAPENIA IS BETTER SUITED ... however SARCOPENIA IS ALREADY A WIDELY RECOGNISED TERM, SO REPLACING IT MIGHT LEAD TO FURTHER CONFUSION`), `buck2011` (`a PRAGMATIC COMPROMISE between IUPAC/CAS nomenclature, internal consistency and existing LEGACY USAGE`) and `bronte2016` (`THE TERM MDSC MAY NOT BE OPTIMAL ... The fourth I counted was `staab2017` keeping PPV, SMD, VV and CSD as ICD-11 INDEX TERMS - preserving RETIRED names as cross-references, which is not keeping a suboptimal term IN USE. A different act, and counting it was the error. span.label: differentiating conditions —distinct-from→ risk factors
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `RATHER THAN USING EXCLUSIONARY CRITERIA in the definition of language disorder, WE DRAW A THREEFOLD DISTINCTION BETWEEN DIFFERENTIATING CONDITIONS, RISK FACTORS AND CO-OCCURRING CONDITIONS.` The distinction exists because the old single category was being used administratively: `exclusionary criteria WERE SOMETIMES INTERPRETED AS CRITERIA FOR DENYING SERVICES TO CHILDREN`
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: pragmatic impairment —is-a→ language disorder
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `First, in DSM-5, SPCD IS SEEN AS A NEW CATEGORY OF NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER, WHEREAS WE REGARD PRAGMATICS AS PART OF LANGUAGE, AND HENCE PRAGMATIC IMPAIRMENT AS A TYPE OF LANGUAGE DISORDER.` Two manuals, one phenomenon, and the disagreement is about WHICH TREE IT HANGS FROM rather than about the child - and the practical consequence given is which intervention the child is routed to
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: pragmatics —part-of→ language
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `WE REGARD PRAGMATICS AS PART OF LANGUAGE.` The paper's own reason for declining the DSM-5 term, and it is a MEREOLOGICAL claim doing diagnostic work: if pragmatics is part of language then a pragmatic impairment is inside DLD, and if it is a separate social faculty then it is not. **The child's route through the service depends on a part-whole judgement about a construct**
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
